item.title: CNIPA and MIIT to Focus on Strengthening IP Protection in the Photovoltaic Industry

item.title: How Marketers Must Comply with FTC Consumer Review Rule Prohibition on Insider Consumer Reviews
item.description: As previously covered here, the Federal Trade Commission has recently warned businesses to comply with the FTC Consumer Review Rule. On December 22, 2025, the FTC announced that it sent warning letters to alert a number of companies of potential violations of the Rule on the Use of Consumer Reviews and Testimonials (the “Consumer Review Rule”). The letters warn of potential violations of the agency’s Rule, which prohibits certain deceptive or unfair conduct related to the use of product reviews

item.title: Recent Developments in Artificial Intelligence and Privacy Legislation in New York State
item.description: New York State’s 2025 legislative session marked a notable moment in the evolution of artificial intelligence (AI) and privacy regulation. item.title: The “Disparate” Dilemma in Employment Discrimination Litigation [Video]

item.title: CNIPA Revokes Four Chinese Patent Firms’ Licenses for Fabricating Applicants Using Stolen Personal Data
item.description: On January 4, 2026, China’s National Intellectual Property Administration (CNIPA) announced it had revoked 4 Chinese patent firms’ licenses for filing ‘irregular’ patent applications using fabricated patent applicants based on stolen personal data. The firms in question had purchased stolen personal data from a Xu XX, who had been sentenced to 3.5 years in prison in May 2025.
